chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except in the well-known matters in which they share with disbelievers and hypocrites, namely eating, drinking, marriage, and enjoyment. Wherever he finds negligence, anger, or forgetfulness in them, he exerts power over them, thereby removing them from guardianship to opposition, from faith to disbelief, from obedience to disobedience, from nearness to distance, from light to darkness, from life to death, from safety to destruction, from success to loss, and from Paradise to Hellfire.
He said: And this is His saying, the Exalted: 'His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate him with Allah.'

key_terms.الْخِلَافَةُ: Opposition or divergence from divine will

ai.seo_question: How does Satan gain authority over believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's dominion is not absolute but conditional, extending primarily to the physical and worldly realms such as eating, drinking, and marriage. This authority is activated specifically when believers exhibit negligence, anger, or forgetfulness, causing a slip from obedience to sin, a mechanism distinct from the initial call to faith. This nuanced view underscores the Shia understanding of *fitrah* (innate disposition) remaining intact unless obscured by heedlessness in daily conduct.
